properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It came from the dev_reflow2 two-agent exercise, 2026-09-28/29 (art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, items D10 and I15). The owner agent set closure at 100% on all five legs and ruled: "'design done' may close a budget on an estimate marked as asserted. 'Build done' requires every budget to close on a measurement." The report then read traceability 0/7, and seams and decisions null. Anthony asked for every idea from the report to be brainstormed (2026-09-29).

WHAT IS SETTLED AND NOT REOPENED HERE: dec:idea-a-design-closes-and-the-design-says-when (accepted), where closure is a report against a declared threshold. Its own words are the SE meaning: "A design that closes can be built". What is open is only HOW the pre-build reading is computed, since the build shipped with the delivery line as its only traceability predicate (see the finding beside this node).

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) A DECLARED PHASE ON THE CRITERION, `closure_phase: design | build`.
  - design: traceability means a requirement is satisfied by a capability that is allocated and has a planned check; budgets close on any stated basis; seams need both sides specified; decisions need no open decision governing planned work.
  - build: today's delivery line, and budgets must close on measured contributions.
  One knob. It maps to systems engineering's design reviews against its test and audit reviews. Counter: "design done" printed beside a red build can be quoted as "done".
(b) A BASIS PER LEG: each counted leg declares what counts ("traceability: planned | delivered", "budgets: any | measured"). Most flexible. Counter: five more knobs, and a combination nobody asked for (delivered traceability with estimated budgets) becomes sayable.
(c) TWO CRITERIA ON ONE PROJECT, design closure and build closure, both always reported. Counter: two verdicts to keep straight. It is (a) with both answers shown at once, which may be its strength.
(d) VERIFICATION METHOD DECIDES, with no new knob: at design time a check whose method is analysis or inspection and whose status is passing closes traceability. Counter: an analysis marked passing on an unbuilt design is the unevidenced claim the provenance leg exists to catch.
(e) KEEP CLOSURE = BUILD and add a separate design-completeness read. Counter: the owner asked for design-done AS closure; a second report splits the answer.

AND ONE SIBLING, whichever option: a PARKED requirement was the first traceability hole on the ikg design, because closure does not read parking either. Whether a parked requirement leaves the population or is counted separately (as detect_defects counts swept.parked) belongs with this.

RANKING, as a finding: (a) or (c) is the smallest honest change; (d) costs nothing and weakens what "passing" means; (b) is (a) with more surface.
properties.name: OPEN — HOW should closure read "design done" as well as "build done"? A design that is fully allocated and traced, with checks planned and budgets closing on estimates, reads 0% on traceability today because the leg is the delivery line. Should closure take a declared phase, a basis per leg, two criteria, or verification-by-analysis?
properties.rationale: The accepted closure decision said what closing means. This asks only how its pre-build half is computed, because the only computation it could reuse was the build half.
